transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: THE ILO DIGITAL LABOUR PLATFORM POLICY TRACKER, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a global policy database that monitors how countries regulate platform work through legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions.' Coverage ('more than 30 countries'), eight issues, its audience, and two related initiatives: the Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193) and the Observatory on AI and Work. Five cards, three of them the ILO's.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview defines the tracker, lists the issues it covers and places it among the ILO's platform-economy work, from the ILO's pages.
findings: THE TRACKER HELD. The eight issues (employment status, remuneration, algorithms, working time, data, safety, termination, collective bargaining) and the audience are the record's; the CBA component is its addition of 7 November 2025. Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

JUDICIAL DECISIONS AHEAD OF THE TRACKER. The tracker's home page (card 1) states the aim, 'a comprehensive overview of global policies, legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions', and in the next sentences its limit: 'Currently, the tracker focuses on legislative developments worldwide, and includes collective bargaining agreements which are publicly available in Europe. The tracker will further develop ... the judicial decisions.' The composition turns the aim into the present and drops the limit; the ILO's expansion page gives the decisions as the next phase.

'MORE THAN 30 COUNTRIES'. Held at the card's grain: the tracker's home page (card 1) lists 33 countries, with 58 legislation records, 15 collective bargaining agreements and 11 other initiatives (counted in session from its grid). The record states no count.

THE CONVENTION. 'Decent Work in the Platform Economy Convention, 2026 (No. 193)' rests on the ILO's digital labour platforms card; the record, compiled from the tracker's launch and expansion pages and the Observatory page, does not carry it. A record change to check against the ILO's own text.
TWO ISSUES ADDED. 'Remuneration and fair pay' and 'Contract termination and account deactivation' carry 'fair pay' and 'account deactivation', which no field source gives among the tracked issues.
analysis: A policy tracker is composed a phase ahead of itself. The record's limit (coverage still expanding; decisions planned) is the line the composition crosses, and its new instrument, the Convention, is one the record should carry once read from the ILO.
per_note: The ILO named; no person; no identifier; the ILO's own pages cited.

read.notes: Claim boundary absent: the scope is inflated. The composition says it monitors regulation 'through legislation, collective bargaining agreements, and judicial decisions', but judicial decisions are the stated next phase, not yet integrated (census: 'NOT a court-decision database yet'); and 'Tracks policy developments, laws, and agreements across more than 30 countries' gives a count the records do not state (the application was not saved; the CBA component covers the European Union). Purpose present: 'support evidence-based policymaking' for governments and social partners is the launch page's 'facilitate social dialogue and evidence-based policymaking'. No date (14 August 2025; 7 November 2025). Deposit chain absent: the phased chain (launch, CBA component, planned judicial decisions) is not carried; the planned phase is composed as present. The Convention 'No. 193' of 2026 comes from card 3 (an ILO page) and lies outside the records; set beside the tracker, not merged. No inversion, no standing substitution.
